title: Shirvan
capsule: Shirvan was a long-lived polity occupying the eastern Caucasus corridor between the Greater Caucasus and the Caspian Sea, roughly corresponding to the northern half of modern Azerbaijan. The Shirvanshah dynasty, of claimed Sassanid descent, maintained authority through Arab conquest, Mongol suzerainty, and Timurid overlordship, producing a notable cultural florescence in the 12th–14th centuries including the construction of the Palace of the Shirvanshahs in Baku (a UNESCO World Heritage site). The Shirvanshah state was extinguished in 1538–1539 when the Safavid Shah Tahmasp I suppressed a local revolt and incorporated the region directly into Safavid Iran.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core political geography is well-attested from Arabic and Persian sources; exact boundaries fluctuated and peripheral areas—particularly southward toward Arran—remain imprecisely mapped for many periods.
